claims.text: AP2, the Agent Payments Protocol, defines signed mandates that record what a user authorized an agent to buy or pay.
AP2 is not a payment rail; it carries authorization evidence on top of existing payment methods such as cards, bank transfers and stablecoins.
AP2 is not A2A; v0.2 describes AP2 as a security feature inside a commerce protocol, and A2A is only one transport used by its samples.
Google created the GitHub repository google-agentic-commerce/AP2 on 2025-05-30.
The AP2 repository is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
The public AP2 repository is exported by Copybara from Google's internal third_party/ap2 tree, according to its METADATA file.
Google announced AP2 on 2025-09-16 in a Google Cloud blog post by Stavan Parikh and Rao Surapaneni.
The launch post said AP2 was developed with more than 60 organizations.

The launch post named Adyen, American Express, Ant International, Coinbase, Etsy, Forter, Intuit, JCB, Mastercard, Mysten Labs, PayPal, Revolut, Salesforce, ServiceNow, UnionPay International and Worldpay as collaborators.
Visa does not appear in the AP2 launch post or in any version of the AP2 partners page.
At launch, AP2 was described as usable as an extension of the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Google donated AP2 to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28, announced in a post by Stavan Parikh, VP and GM of Payments.
Google's donation post says moving ownership to FIDO keeps AP2 platform-agnostic and community-led.
Mastercard contributed its Verifiable Intent framework to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28, describing it as co-developed with Google and designed to work with AP2.
On 2026-04-28 the FIDO Alliance described its Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group as newly formed, chaired by members from CVS Health, Google and OpenAI.
The FIDO Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group is vice-chaired by members from Amazon, Google and Okta.
FIDO's Payments Technical Working Group, chaired by members from Mastercard and Visa, is where the AP2 and Verifiable Intent contributions are to be developed.
The FIDO Payments group was not new in 2026: FIDO launched a Payments Working Group on 2025-04-29, co-chaired by Henna Kapur of Visa and Jonathan Grossar of Mastercard.
Only the Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group was newly formed on 2026-04-28; the payments group already existed.
The FIDO Alliance gave no deliverable or date for the AP2 work, saying only that it will report as the work progresses.
No FIDO specification or public draft based on AP2 was found as of 2026-10-11.
Governance of the AP2 specification now sits with FIDO Alliance working groups, not with Google alone.
The AP2 FAQ says core specification work will continue in FIDO while Google keeps improving the code samples and SDK.
On 2026-05-27 an AP2 specification author wrote on issue 268 that further iterations had officially moved to FIDO.
The ap2-protocol.org site says standardization continues in FIDO's Agentic Authentication Technical and Payments Technical Working Groups.
AP2 v0.1.0 was released on GitHub on 2025-09-16 from commit bb57b6b.
AP2 v0.2.0 was released on GitHub on 2026-04-28 from commit b4587ac, the merge of PR 233.
The last commit on the AP2 main branch is e1ea56d, dated 2026-04-29.
No commit was merged to the AP2 main branch between 2026-04-29 and 2026-10-11.
Between 2026-04-29 and 2026-10-11, 44 issues and 63 pull requests were opened on the AP2 repository and none of the pull requests was merged.
AP2 v0.2 has no Intent Mandate and no Cart Mandate; it defines only Checkout and Payment Mandates.
AP2 v0.1 defined three mandates in Pydantic models: IntentMandate, CartMandate and PaymentMandate.
AP2 v0.1 used the data keys ap2.mandates.IntentMandate, ap2.mandates.CartMandate and ap2.mandates.PaymentMandate.
Each AP2 v0.2 mandate type carries a vct value with a numeric version suffix, and implementations must match the exact string including the suffix.
The AP2 v0.2 specification document is titled Agentic Payment Protocol (v0.2), while the project elsewhere uses the name Agent Payments Protocol.
The AP2 partners page had 56 entries at launch, 113 after 2025-10-30 and 125 at its last edit on 2026-02-09, and v0.2 removed it.
Tether, Solana and OKX were added to the AP2 partners page on 2025-10-30 (PR 103).
x402 payment method support was added to the AP2 Python human-in-the-loop samples on 2025-12-15 (PR 121).
AP2 v0.2 defines five roles: Shopping Agent, Credential Provider, Merchant, Merchant Payment Processor and Trusted Surface.
In AP2, MPP stands for Merchant Payment Processor, a role, and is unrelated to the Machine Payments Protocol.
The AP2 v0.2 Trusted Surface must be non-agentic, and the Shopping Agent is expected to be agentic.
AP2 v0.2 requires all validation by any role to run in deterministic code, whether or not the role is agentic.
Merchant, Merchant Payment Processor and Credential Provider may be agentic or non-agentic in AP2 v0.2.
AP2 lets one entity play several or all roles, and any role may delegate its verification duties to another party.
AP2 v0.1 listed six roles: User, User Agent or Shopping Agent, Credentials Provider, Remote or Merchant Endpoint, Merchant Payment Processor Endpoint, and Network and Issuer.
AP2 defines two mandate delegation models: User Credential and Trusted Agent Provider.
In the Trusted Agent Provider model the agent provider signs mandates with a key the agent must not be able to access or use without the Trusted Surface.
AP2's Trusted Agent Provider is a delegation model and is unrelated to Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol.
AP2 lists a digital wallet, a payment network, or an instrument store run by the agent or the merchant as possible Credential Providers.
The closed Checkout Mandate schema requires vct, checkout_jwt and checkout_hash and allows iat and exp.
The closed Checkout Mandate vct is the constant mandate.checkout.1.
checkout_jwt is a base64url-encoded, merchant-signed JWT of the Checkout payload and is selectively disclosable.
checkout_hash is the base64url hash of checkout_jwt, using the _sd_alg algorithm if present and sha-256 otherwise.
When AP2 is used with UCP, checkout_jwt must contain the UCP Checkout object.
The open Checkout Mandate schema requires vct (constant mandate.checkout.open.1), constraints and cnf.
An open Checkout Mandate's constraints array must contain at least one checkout.line_items constraint.
The closed Payment Mandate schema defines vct, transaction_id, payee, pisp, payment_amount, payment_instrument, execution_date, risk_data, iat and exp.
The closed Payment Mandate requires vct, transaction_id, payee, payment_amount and payment_instrument; pisp, execution_date, risk_data, iat and exp are optional.
The closed Payment Mandate vct is the constant mandate.payment.1.
transaction_id in the Payment Mandate is the base64url hash of the checkout_jwt value, which binds the payment to one checkout.
payment_amount holds a currency code and an integer amount in ISO 4217 minor units, for example 27999 for 279.99 USD.
risk_data in a Payment Mandate is a map of risk signals collected by the Trusted Surface when the mandate is created.
An absent execution_date in a Payment Mandate means immediate execution.
The open Payment Mandate schema requires vct (constant mandate.payment.open.1), constraints and cnf, and its constraints must include a payment.reference constraint.
cnf in an open mandate is the RFC 7800 confirmation claim that holds the agent's public key.
The AP2 v0.2 checkout constraint types are checkout.allowed_merchants and checkout.line_items.

The AP2 v0.2 payment constraint types are payment.agent_recurrence, payment.allowed_payees, payment.allowed_payment_instruments, payment.allowed_pisps, payment.amount_range, payment.budget, payment.execution_date and payment.reference.
payment.amount_range requires currency and max, with optional min, all amounts in integer minor units.
payment.budget caps the total spent across recurring uses and is meant to be used with payment.agent_recurrence.
payment.agent_recurrence frequency takes one of ON_DEMAND, DAILY, WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY or ANNUALLY, with optional max_occurrences.
payment.reference carries conditional_transaction_id, the digest of the associated open Checkout Mandate.
payment.execution_date constrains execution to a window given by optional not_before and not_after.
The checkout.line_items constraint is met only if each requirement is matched by checkout items without reusing any item, and AP2 suggests a maximum-flow algorithm to check it.
An AP2 verifier must treat any unknown constraint type as failing evaluation.
New AP2 constraints need a unique type, a schema marking selectively disclosable fields, and an evaluation algorithm.
The AP2 PISP type requires legal_name, brand_name and domain_name, and describes domain_name as secured by the eIDAS QWAC certificate of the TPP.
The AP2 Merchant type requires id and name and allows website; the Payment Instrument type requires id and type and allows description.
The AP2 JWK type fixes kty to EC, crv to P-256 and alg to ES256.
The Payment Receipt schema requires status, iss, iat, reference and payment_id, plus psp_confirmation_id and network_confirmation_id on success, and error and error_description on error.
The Checkout Receipt schema requires status, iss, iat and reference, plus order_id on success, and error and error_description on error.
A receipt's reference is the hash of the closed mandate it binds to, computed the same way as sd_hash.
AP2 defines four action authorization errors: invalid_credential, unresolved_constraint, invalid_mandate and mandates_not_supported.
invalid_credential and invalid_mandate are terminal errors, while unresolved_constraint and mandates_not_supported may signal a fallback.
The v0.1 IntentMandate had fields user_cart_confirmation_required, natural_language_description, merchants, skus, requires_refundability and intent_expiry.
The v0.1 CartMandate wrapped CartContents, including a W3C PaymentRequest, and an optional merchant_authorization JWT whose payload included cart_hash.
The v0.1 PaymentMandate held payment_mandate_contents and an optional user_authorization, a verifiable presentation such as an SD-JWT VC with a key-binding JWT over the mandate hashes.
In the AP2 Human Present flow the user directly approves the closed Checkout and Payment Mandates on a Trusted Surface.
In the Human Present flow the Credential Provider verifies the Payment Mandate and creates a payment token, possibly getting a scoped credential from the network.

In the Human Present flow the Merchant checks the Checkout Mandate against the current cart and the Merchant Payment Processor checks the Payment Mandate in the token and its checkout_jwt hash binding.
The Merchant Payment Processor returns a signed Payment Receipt to the Shopping Agent, Credential Provider and Network, and the Merchant returns a signed Checkout Receipt to the Shopping Agent.
In the AP2 Human Not Present flow the user signs open Checkout and Payment Mandates that include the agent's public key in cnf.
In the Human Not Present flow the agent later signs closed mandates with its own key, and sd_hash binds each closed mandate to its open parent.
An AP2 Shopping Agent must not present a new closed mandate from the same open mandate until it receives a rejection receipt for the previous one.
AP2 recommends setting exp on open mandates to the smallest value that lets the agent complete its task.
Verifiers always receive closed Checkout and Payment Mandates in both modes; only the way the signature is trusted differs.
A Human Not Present flow can become a Human Present flow when the Merchant or Credential Provider returns unresolved_constraint and the user is brought back to approve closed mandates.
AP2 dispute verification recomputes the checkout_jwt hash, checks both receipt references against the closed mandates, and verifies both mandates.
AP2 leaves dispute retention, retrieval and adjudication outside the specification.
For User Credential delegation, an AP2 agent places an object with type delegate, format and delegate_payload in the OpenID4VP transaction_data array.
AP2 recommends using the Digital Credentials API for OpenID4VP delegation where available.
The AP2 delegation example requests a credential with vct com.emvco.dpc and discloses card_last_four, card_network_code and credential_id.
AP2 v0.2 defines two mandate states: open, bound to an agent key with constraints, and closed, bound to one transaction.
After a success receipt, the AP2 agent stores the open mandate, closed mandate and receipt together and narrows the open mandate's scope.
AP2 v0.2 leaves catalog, checkout and role-to-role APIs to the surrounding commerce protocol and is designed to be compatible with UCP.
The AP2 Python and Go samples run the roles as A2A agents, with card and x402 scenarios for both human-present and human-not-present modes.
UCP carries AP2 through the capability dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate, which extends dev.ucp.shopping.checkout and is advertised in /.well-known/ucp.
In UCP the merchant's signature sits in ap2.merchant_authorization, the user's Checkout Mandate in ap2.checkout_mandate, and the Payment Mandate in payment.instruments[*].credential.token.
AP2 v0.2 secures mandates as SD-JWT VCs and chains them with the Delegate SD-JWT individual draft.
The Delegate SD-JWT draft was posted to the IETF as draft-gco-oauth-delegate-sd-jwt-00 on 2026-04-22.
AP2 v0.2 uses SD-JWT VC, OpenID4VP and the Digital Credentials API; W3C VC 2.0 and DIDs are part of the wider credential family, not dependencies of the spec.
Every AP2 v0.2 mandate example uses ES256 signatures.
AP2's specification requires the Checkout JWT to use a non-deterministic signature such as ECDSA rather than a deterministic one such as Ed25519, to prevent rainbow-table guessing of checkout_hash.
AP2's security considerations allow a deterministic signature for the Checkout JWT if the Checkout carries a salt of sufficient entropy, which conflicts with the specification text.
Issue 268, opened 2026-05-26, reports the signature-determinism conflict and was still open on 2026-10-11.
AP2 cites SD-JWT as RFC 9901 dated February 2025, but the RFC Editor dates RFC 9901 to November 2025.
AP2 assumes prompt injection cannot be prevented and treats every LLM and agent as a potential attacker.
AP2 v0.2 defines no way to revoke a mandate before it expires.
AP2 v0.2 specifies no step-up authentication; a failed check falls back through the unresolved_constraint error.
AP2 v0.1 let any party require a redirect challenge such as 3DS2 or an OTP during payment.
AP2 leaves liability to the payment networks; v0.1 offered an evidence table that it called a guide, not a binding contract.
The AP2 v0.2 Executive Summary still mentions 3DS2 challenges, although the normative v0.2 documents define no challenge mechanism.
AP2 releases the payment token to the merchant only after a final Payment Mandate is verified, to limit token theft.
AP2 requires salted SD-JWT digests and allows decoy digests to protect privacy.
AP2 leaves agent identification to the commerce protocol layer.
No CVE or GitHub security advisory was found for the AP2 repository as of 2026-10-11.
Outside contributors have reported unmerged bugs in the AP2 SDK and samples, including that verifiers never consume an accepted Payment Mandate (issue 346).
AP2 natively supports spending caps through payment.amount_range and payment.budget.
AP2 natively supports merchant and payee scoping through checkout.allowed_merchants, payment.allowed_payees, payment.allowed_pisps and payment.allowed_payment_instruments.
AP2 defines no agent registry or know-your-agent mechanism.
AP2 lets Credential Providers, networks or processors reject overlapping mandates or invalidate previously issued tokens.
AP2 defines no public registry, explorer, indexer, event stream or .well-known path of its own.
AP2 JSON Schema identifiers live under https://ap2-protocol.org/schemas/.
The AP2 glossary defines Strong Customer Authentication, Dynamic Linking and PISP, terms from European payment regulation, without claiming PSD2 compliance.
The AP2 FAQ says the design keeps sensitive PCI and PII data away from shopping agents through payload encryption and selective disclosure.
The AP2 Python SDK lives in the repository as package ap2 version 0.1 and is not published by Google to PyPI.
The PyPI package named ap2 and the npm package named ap2 belong to unrelated third parties, not Google.
The AP2 repository contains samples in Python, Go and Android plus a Vite and React web client.
A proposed AP2 TypeScript SDK (PR 305) was closed without merging on 2026-10-03.
Production use of AP2 mandates is unverified anywhere, including inside UCP.
One third party, Suede Agent Studio, self-reported a merchant-side AP2 v0.2 deployment in issue 345 on 2026-08-29; this is not independently verified.
draft-stone-vcap-ap2-binding-01, an individual Informational Internet-Draft by Ben Stone of SwarmSync.AI, was posted on 2026-09-04.
The VCAP-AP2 binding draft's abstract still names the v0.1 IntentMandate, CartMandate and PaymentMandate objects.
The AP2 repository had 3,216 stars and 510 forks on 2026-10-11.
AP2 defines no protocol fee; costs are those of the underlying payment rail.
UCP's initial commit on 2026-01-11 already contained an AP2 mandates extension document.
UCP's 2026-08-25 refactor and release v2026-08-25 reference AP2 v0.2 and AP2 issue 268.
The a2a-x402 extension launched with AP2 on 2025-09-16, built with Coinbase, the Ethereum Foundation and MetaMask.
The a2a-x402 v0.2 spec supports a Standalone Flow and an Embedded Flow that nests x402 objects inside higher-level protocols such as AP2.
The a2a-x402 v0.2 embedding targets the AP2 v0.1 CartMandate and PaymentMandate, which do not match AP2 v0.2, where no Cart mandate exists.
a2a-x402 tracks payment state in x402.payment.status with values payment-required, payment-submitted, payment-rejected, payment-verified, payment-completed and payment-failed.
The a2a-x402 v0.1 spec does not mention AP2.
Verifiable Intent uses the same mandate vct values as AP2 v0.2: mandate.checkout.open.1, mandate.checkout.1, mandate.payment.open.1 and mandate.payment.1.
AP2 and Verifiable Intent have aligned constraint semantics but different key prefixes: AP2 uses payment.amount_range while Verifiable Intent uses mandate.payment.amount_range.

Verifiable Intent's spec README uses mandate.checkout.allowed_merchants, mandate.checkout.line_items, mandate.payment.allowed_payees, mandate.payment.budget, mandate.payment.agent_recurrence and mandate.payment.reference, and adds mandate.payment.recurrence.
The AP2 repository does not reference ERC-8004, Visa TAP, OpenAI ACP, Shared Payment Tokens or the Machine Payments Protocol.
ERC-8226 Regulated Agent Mandate is a Draft ERC created on 2026-04-12 by Brickken authors that lets a verified principal grant an agent scoped, time-bounded and capped authority on chain.
ERC-8226 includes on-chain revocation and freeze functions such as revokeMandate and freezeAgent, which AP2 lacks, and names ERC-8004 as its agent identity layer.
ERC-8226 does not mention AP2.
AP2's Mandate Receipt prose uses a result field while the receipt schemas use status, a mismatch reported in issue 374 on 2026-10-11.
AP2's amount_range example uses decimal values such as 100.50, while the schema types the field as integer minor units.
AP2's security document writes mandate.payment.reference while the schema key is payment.reference.
AP2 schema descriptions say vct must be mandate.checkout or mandate.payment while the constants carry a .1 suffix.
arXiv:2608.23858 (2026-08-24) catalogs 48 threats to AP2 v0.2, eight of which reach the High band in at least one deployment architecture.
The authors of arXiv:2608.23858 built their own testbed because no complete public AP2 deployment was available.
arXiv:2602.06345 (2026-02-06) analyzes replay and context-binding gaps in the AP2 mandate lifecycle and proposes consume-once runtime nonces.
arXiv:2601.22569 (2026-01-30) shows prompt injection attacks, named Branded Whisper and Vault Whisper, against an AP2-based shopping agent.
arXiv:2609.00060 (2026-08-30) models x402, MPP, ACP and AP2 in Tamarin and reports 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency findings across 86 verification cases.
The AP2 README links an Agent Factory podcast episode from September 2025 titled Agent payments, can you do my shopping?
On 2026-05-19 Google said it would begin bringing AP2 to Google products in the coming months, starting with Gemini Spark.

Verifiable Intent renamed its constraint keys and added .1 suffixes to its mandate vct values on main on 2026-04-20 (PR 23) without a version bump; at tag v0.1.0 the names were, for example, payment.amount and payment.allowed_payee.
The UCP extension that carries AP2 was named dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate from v2026-01-11 through v2026-04-08 and was renamed dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate in v2026-08-25.

The UCP AP2 extension defines its own error codes: mandate_required, agent_missing_key, mandate_invalid_signature, mandate_expired, mandate_scope_mismatch, merchant_authorization_invalid and merchant_authorization_missing.

In UCP the merchant signs the checkout as a JWS with detached content in ap2.merchant_authorization, using ES256, ES384 or ES512, JCS canonicalization and keys published in keys[] of /.well-known/ucp.

arXiv:2609.11757 reports that AP2 signs the completed transaction but not the decisions that led to it, so product-description text can steer a sample shopping agent, and proposes a session-binding defense called A-VIP.
In the a2a-x402 Embedded Flow the x402PaymentRequiredResponse sits inside an AP2 CartMandate in task.artifacts, and the signed PaymentPayload sits inside an AP2 PaymentMandate in message.parts.
The a2a-x402 repository ships a Python package named x402-a2a at version 0.1.0, authored by Coinbase Developer Platform and Google A2A, and that package was not found on PyPI on 2026-10-11.
An open Payment Mandate may pre-set payee, payment_amount, payment_instrument, pisp, execution_date and risk_data; the closed mandate made from it must carry every field its schema requires.
Once the AP2 extension is negotiated in UCP the checkout session is security locked, and neither party may fall back to an unprotected checkout.
The AP2 OpenID4VP delegation example uses response_mode dc_api and ES256 for both the SD-JWT and the key-binding JWT.
In the human-not-present mode the closed mandate is a key-binding JWT signed with the agent key named in cnf, and its sd_hash covers the user-signed open mandate it extends.
A Mandate Receipt is a Verifier-signed JWT whose iss, result and reference are required, with optional error and error_description.

When any Merchant check fails the Merchant must return a Checkout Receipt JWT with the error, and when a Credential Provider or Network check fails they must return a Payment Receipt JWT with the error.

AP2 lists the Shopping Agent or Merchant as possible providers of the Checkout Mandate and Receipt in a dispute, and the Shopping Agent, Credential Provider, Network or Merchant Payment Processor for the Payment Mandate and Receipt; it suggests a future retrieval keyed on transaction_id.

The AP2 specification notes that because the user approves the closed checkout in the human-present mode, that mode can often be replaced by a traditional e-commerce journey between the Merchant and the Trusted Surface.
For payment methods that push funds, the AP2 Merchant receives confirmation that funds were sent instead of initiating a charge.
An AP2 Shopping Agent must present only the open-mandate disclosures needed to evaluate the closed mandates.
AP2 v0.2 says delegation from one Shopping Agent to another is conceptually possible but outside the scope of the specification.
AP2 lists a deterministic part of the agent application, a standalone wallet or issuer app, or a trusted user agent such as a mobile platform or browser as possible Trusted Surfaces.
The AP2 Python SDK requires Python 3.11 or later and depends on sd-jwt 0.10.4 and jwcrypto 1.5.6.
AP2 v0.1 documented an A2A extension with the sample extension URI https://google-a2a.github.io/A2A/ext/payments/v1.
The a2a-x402 v0.2 extension URI is https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/a2a-x402/blob/main/spec/v0.2.
The AP2 checkout.line_items constraint does not allow one open mandate to be split across several checkouts.
payment.budget types max as a number with no stated unit and its documentation example uses 1000.00, so the budget unit is unresolved in v0.2.
The implementer in AP2 issue 345 publishes /.well-known/ap2.json and /.well-known/ap2-jwks.json, paths that the AP2 specification does not define.
The AP2 FAQ describes the UCP AP2 extension as something merchants will be able to use for agent-driven transactions, not as a live deployment.
The ap2-protocol.org site still describes AP2 as an extension for A2A and UCP.

ERC-8226 defines mandate fields such as validFrom, validUntil, maxTransactionValue, maxCumulativeValue, cumulativeUsed and revoked, and functions such as grantMandate, revokeMandate, extendMandate, canExecute, recordExecution and freezeAgent.
arXiv:2608.23858 finds that a valid mandate signature does not guarantee that a transaction reflects user intent when the context before authorization was manipulated.
In AP2 v0.1 the human-not-present path had the user sign a detailed Intent Mandate up front, after which the agent could generate a Cart Mandate when the conditions were met.
The AP2 Merchant Payment Processor must verify that the payment credential is scoped to the checkout, for example by finding the closed Payment Mandate inside the credential.
The AP2 Merchant must check that the hash of the Checkout JWT it sent matches checkout_hash and, when open Checkout Mandates are included, evaluate every constraint.
To verify a mandate chain, an AP2 verifier processes the SD-JWT chain under Delegate SD-JWT, checks that the closed mandate keeps every value the open mandate fixed, and evaluates each constraint.
The AP2 item type says it matches the UCP item type of 2026-04-08, with required id, title and price in integer minor units.
In the Trusted Agent Provider model, verifiers trust a list of agent providers instead of a user credential issuer.
The AP2 Python SDK README describes MandateClient methods create, present and verify, and computes a receipt reference as the SHA-256 of the closed leaf JWT.

The FIDO Alliance press release of 2026-04-28 calls the payments group the Payments Technical Working Group, while its 2025-04-29 release named it the Payments Working Group; no source says whether the name changed.
AP2 v0.1 offered liability guidance in a table of evidence per failure scenario and said each network defines its own liability rules.
Ant International, Mastercard and Visa announced Know Your Agent interoperability work on 2026-09-11, building on Visa TAP and Mastercard Verifiable Intent; it is a collaboration, not a network rule.
